proposals.before: Her father Chen Sui rose repeatedly to the post of Grand Preceptor under the Five Dynasties.
proposals.after: Her father Chen Xing rose repeatedly to the post of Minister over the Masses (situ) under the Five Dynasties.
proposals.reason: Chinese 父陘 names him Xing (陘), not Sui; 司徒 is situ (Minister over the Masses), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: Her father Chen Sui repeatedly held the office of Grand Preceptor during the Five Dynasties period.
proposals.after: Her father Chen Xing repeatedly held the office of situ (Minister over the Masses) during the Five Dynasties period.
proposals.reason: Same errors as the idiomatic line: 陘 is Xing, and 司徒 is not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Nu, known by the childhood name Yixin, was the daughter of the State Uncle and Princess Consort Taosuwo.
proposals.after: Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Nu, known by the childhood name Yixin, was the daughter of the State Uncle and Commandant-escort (imperial son-in-law) Taosuwo.
proposals.reason: 駙馬都尉 is the imperial son-in-law office (commandant-escort), not 'Princess Consort'.

proposals.before: The wife of Yelü Nu, Lady Xiao, childhood name Yixin, daughter of the State Uncle and Princess Consort Taosuwo.
proposals.after: The wife of Yelü Nu, Lady Xiao, childhood name Yixin, daughter of the State Uncle and Commandant-escort Taosuwo.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise mistranslates 駙馬都尉 as Princess Consort.

decisions.reason: s0009 父陘 names the father Xing (陘), not Sui, and 累官司徒 is successive appointment to situ (Minister over the Masses), not Grand Preceptor (太師). The proposed English corrects both errors.
The literal line repeats the same mistakes: 陘 is Xing and 司徒 is situ, not Grand Preceptor. The proposed replacement matches the Chinese.
國舅駙馬都尉陶蘇斡 marks Taosuwo as State Uncle and commandant-escort (imperial son-in-law); 駙馬都尉 is not a princess consort title. The repair restores the correct office.
